First successful FortiGate admin/SSL-VPN login from never-seen ASN after failure burst AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the post-spray foothold step from the Feb 2026 campaign: the first-ever successful FortiGate authentication from an ASN/geo that had only failures in the baseline window. AWS confirmed 600+ devices fell to this exact shape across 55+ countries. Rationale: Grounded in the article's 'AWS confirmed 600+ devices across 55+ countries' line and the kill-chain hint that first-time-seen ASN+success-after-failure-burst is the campaign's signature. Anti-baseline join is the canonical first-seen detection shape.
ATT&CKT1133 T1078
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Roaming admin connecting from a new hotel / airport ASN they've never used before
  • M&A integration where a newly-acquired sub-org logs in to the parent's appliance for the first time
  • MSP onboarding a new customer tenant from previously-unseen jump-host ASN
  • Carrier-grade-NAT shift moves a fleet of mobile clients to a new ASN block overnight
  • DR test from a backup site whose egress IP is not in the 30-day baseline
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<known_roaming_admin_ips>"])) | where SourceUserName !in~ ("msp-onboarding", "dr-test")
Response runbook
1) Triage: enrich the source IP with ASN/geo + threat-intel; pull the preceding 24 h of failures from the same /24; verify the account is genuinely admin/VPN with management access. 2) Contain: kill the active SSL-VPN tunnel, revoke session cookies, disable the account, and isolate the FortiGate management interface from public reach. 3) Hunt: look for config-change / `exec` CLI bursts from this session, outbound HTTPS from the appliance to LLM-API or unknown JSON-RPC endpoints, and any new admin or local user created in the same window.
let Lookback = 30d;
let Recent = 1h;
let KnownASN = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(Recent))
    | where RemotePort in (443, 10443, 4433) and InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("sslvpnd", "httpsd")
    | summarize by RemoteIP;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(Recent)
| where RemotePort in (443, 10443, 4433)
| join kind=leftanti KnownASN on RemoteIP
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 30d;
let Recent = 1h;
let Baseline = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(Recent))
    | where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
    | where DeviceAction has "success" or Message has_any ("login success", "ssl-vpn-login success")
    | summarize by SourceIP;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Recent)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
| where DeviceAction has "success" or Message has_any ("login success", "ssl-vpn-login success")
| where SourceUserName has_any ("admin", "administrator") or Activity has_any ("ssl-vpn", "admin login")
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on SourceIP
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, DeviceExternalID, Activity, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.syslog OR cisco.firewall) @source.product:(fortigate OR FortiGate) @evt.outcome:success (@msg:("login success" OR "ssl-vpn-login") OR @network.destination.port:(443 OR 10443)) @network.user.name:(admin OR administrator OR *vpn*)
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(Authentication.user) as users, values(Authentication.action) as actions from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn) earliest=-30d@d latest=-1h by Authentication.src_ip, Authentication.src_asn, Authentication.app | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | eventstats values(src_asn) as known_asns by app | eval is_baseline=1 | append [| tstats `summariesonly` count as recent_count, values(Authentication.user) as recent_users from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn) Authentication.action=success earliest=-1h by Authentication.src_ip, Authentication.src_asn, Authentication.app, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | eval is_recent=1] | stats max(is_baseline) as seen_before, max(is_recent) as seen_recent, values(recent_users) as recent_users, values(recent_count) as recent_count, values(_time) as recent_time by src_asn, app | where seen_recent=1 AND isnull(seen_before) | table recent_time app src_asn recent_users recent_count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Authentication.user) as users, values(Authentication.action) as actions from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn) earliest=-30d@d latest=-1h by Authentication.src_ip, Authentication.src_asn, Authentication.app | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | eventstats values(src_asn) as known_asns by app | eval is_baseline=1 | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count as recent_count, values(Authentication.user) as recent_users from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn) Authentication.action=success earliest=-1h by Authentication.src_ip, Authentication.src_asn, Authentication.app, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | eval is_recent=1] | stats max(is_baseline) as seen_before, max(is_recent) as seen_recent, values(recent_users) as recent_users, values(recent_count) as recent_count, values(_time) as recent_time by src_asn, app | where seen_recent=1 AND isnull(seen_before) | table recent_time app src_asn recent_users recent_count
Machine-cadence post-auth FortiGate CLI/API calls in single session (MCP-orchestrated) AIInstallation Medium
Targets the Feb 2026 campaign's signature execution behaviour: an authenticated session that issues many FortiGate CLI/API actions sub-second apart — a cadence no human admin produces — because a custom MCP server is autonomously invoking a curated offensive-tool library against the appliance. Rationale: Article: 'bursts of FortiGate CLI/API calls (config read, diagnose, exec) spaced sub-second apart from a single session — a cadence no human admin produces.' Detection encodes that exact rate/burst signal at the session level rather than alerting on individual commands.
ATT&CKT1059 T1106
Data sourcesChange Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • FortiManager pushing a large policy bundle to the appliance during a scheduled change window
  • Backup / config-export tool (FortiAnalyzer collector, rConfig) pulling running-config via API on cron
  • Authorized BAS or pentest agent enumerating the appliance over the REST API
  • Ansible / Terraform deployment run that idempotent-replays hundreds of `config` blocks
  • Initial provisioning of a new appliance where the engineer pastes a multi-hundred-line config script
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<fortimanager_ip>", "<backup_collector_ip>", "<ansible_runner_ip>"]))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the session's source IP and admin account; check whether FortiManager / approved automation source the burst, and pull the actual command sequence. 2) Contain: terminate the active session, revoke the admin's API token, snapshot the running-config and diff against last-known-good, and block the source IP at the management ACL. 3) Hunt: pivot on the admin account for any new policies, route changes, local user creation, or VPN tunnels added in the burst; check egress from the appliance management plane to LLM/MCP endpoints.
let Window = 1m;
let BurstThreshold = 20;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort in (443, 22, 8443) and InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("httpsd", "sshd", "cli")
| summarize Calls = count(), FirstT = min(Timestamp), LastT = max(Timestamp) by RemoteIP, DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, Window)
| extend DurationSec = datetime_diff('second', LastT, FirstT), RatePerSec = todouble(Calls) / (todouble(datetime_diff('second', LastT, FirstT)) + 1)
| where Calls >= BurstThreshold and (RatePerSec >= 2.0 or DurationSec <= 10)
| order by Timestamp desc
let Window = 1m;
let BurstThreshold = 20;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
| where Activity has_any ("config", "exec", "diagnose", "api", "cli") or Message has_any ("exec ", "config ", "diagnose ", "/api/v2/")
| extend SessionKey = strcat(SourceIP, "|", SourceUserName, "|", DeviceExternalID)
| summarize Calls = count(), Cmds = make_set(Activity, 50), FirstT = min(TimeGenerated), LastT = max(TimeGenerated) by SessionKey, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DeviceExternalID, bin(TimeGenerated, Window)
| extend DurationSec = datetime_diff('second', LastT, FirstT)
| extend RatePerSec = todouble(Calls) / (todouble(DurationSec) + 1.0)
| where Calls >= BurstThreshold and (RatePerSec >= 2.0 or DurationSec <= 10)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.syslog OR cisco.firewall) @source.product:(fortigate OR FortiGate) (@msg:(exec* OR config* OR diagnose* OR "/api/v2/") OR @evt.name:(config_change OR cli_command OR api_call))
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Change.object) as distinct_objects, values(Change.command) as commands, values(Change.object) as objects, min(_time) as first_t, max(_time) as last_t from datamodel=Change where (Change.vendor_product="FortiGate" OR Change.app=fortigate) by Change.user, Change.src, Change.session_id, _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | eval duration_s=last_t-first_t, rate_per_s=count/(duration_s+1) | where count>=20 AND (rate_per_s>=2 OR duration_s<=10) | table _time user src session_id count distinct_objects duration_s rate_per_s commands objects
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Change.object) as distinct_objects, values(Change.command) as commands, values(Change.object) as objects, min(_time) as first_t, max(_time) as last_t from datamodel=Change where (Change.vendor_product="FortiGate" OR Change.app=fortigate) by Change.user, Change.src, Change.session_id, _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | eval duration_s=last_t-first_t, rate_per_s=count/(duration_s+1) | where count>=20 AND (rate_per_s>=2 OR duration_s<=10) | table _time user src session_id count distinct_objects duration_s rate_per_s commands objects
Outbound JSON-RPC or LLM-API egress from network appliance / edge device AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the C2 channel from the Feb 2026 campaign: the custom MCP server brokering tasks between the LLM and compromised FortiGate fleet over HTTPS. Network appliances should never originate AI-API traffic; first-seen FQDN to anthropic / openai / bedrock / unknown JSON-RPC endpoints from edge gear is the tell. Rationale: Article: 'a custom MCP server running offensive tools autonomously' brokering between LLM and compromised devices. Detection ground-truths on the unique behavioural shape — edge appliance originating LLM-API HTTPS — which is essentially zero in any baseline. CloudWatch/VPC-Flow path was dropped because the article-specific telemetry lives on the FortiGate / proxy / DNS layer, not in CloudTrail; emitting an invented VPC-Flow query would be noise.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vendor support session where a FortiGate streams telemetry through an OpenAI-fronted vendor diagnostic chatbot
  • Legitimate internal SOAR / chatops integration on an appliance management host that genuinely calls an LLM
  • Captive-portal proxy on the appliance forwarding a user's browser session to an LLM provider (rare)
  • Future Fortinet firmware that ships its own AI assistant phoning home to a vendor LLM endpoint
  • DNS resolver on the appliance answering a recursive query for a downstream client (split-horizon misconfig)
Suppression filter
| where DestinationHostName !in~ ("telemetry.fortinet.com", "<approved_vendor_chatops_host>") | where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<approved_soar_egress_ip>"]))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify which appliance and which management-plane process originated the connection; verify whether the destination FQDN is a known LLM endpoint and whether any vendor change ticket explains it. 2) Contain: block the destination FQDN/IP at the perimeter from all network-appliance source IPs, snapshot the appliance config and running processes, and rotate admin credentials and API tokens on that device. 3) Hunt: correlate with recent admin-login anomalies on the same appliance, look for matching outbound from peer appliances of the same model, and search for inbound JSON-RPC / unusual TLS-SNI patterns that could be the MCP control channel itself.
let LLMHosts = dynamic(["anthropic.com", "api.anthropic.com", "openai.com", "api.openai.com", "bedrock-runtime", "generativelanguage.googleapis.com", "api.mistral.ai", "api.together.xyz", "api.groq.com", "api.deepseek.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort == 443
| where RemoteUrl has_any (LLMHosts) or InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("sslvpnd", "httpsd", "miglogd", "fgfm", "forticron")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe", "brave.exe", "code.exe", "slack.exe", "teams.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let LLMHosts = dynamic(["anthropic.com", "api.anthropic.com", "openai.com", "api.openai.com", "bedrock-runtime", "generativelanguage.googleapis.com", "api.mistral.ai", "api.together.xyz", "api.groq.com", "api.deepseek.com"]);
let ApplianceVendors = dynamic(["Fortinet", "Palo Alto Networks", "Cisco", "Check Point", "SonicWall", "Juniper", "F5"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DeviceVendor in~ (ApplianceVendors)
| where DestinationPort == 443 or ApplicationProtocol has_any ("https", "ssl", "tls")
| where (isnotempty(DestinationHostName) and DestinationHostName has_any (LLMHosts)) or (isnotempty(RequestURL) and RequestURL has_any (LLMHosts)) or (isnotempty(DestinationDnsDomain) and DestinationDnsDomain has_any (LLMHosts))
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceExternalID, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL, Activity, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| union (
    ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (LLMHosts)
    | where SrcHostname has_any ("fgt", "fortigate", "palo", "asa", "ftd", "checkpoint", "srx", "bigip") or DvcHostname has_any ("fgt", "fortigate", "palo", "asa", "ftd", "checkpoint", "srx", "bigip")
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor=EventVendor, DeviceProduct=EventProduct, DeviceExternalID=DvcHostname, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, DestinationIP=DstIpAddr, DestinationPort=int(null), DestinationHostName=DstHostname, DestinationDnsDomain=DnsQuery, RequestURL=tostring(""), Activity=tostring("dns_query"), Message=tostring("")
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Outbound LLM/MCP API call from network appliance
id: 7c6f1c2a-3d6c-4f9e-9e8b-2ad9b3f1f4a1
description: Detects DNS resolution or HTTPS egress from a network appliance / edge device to a known LLM API host (Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, etc.) — these devices should never originate AI traffic and the pattern matches the Feb 2026 MCP-orchestrated FortiGate campaign.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/ai-broke-vulnerability-management-thats.html
author: DexCore
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1102.002
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith:
      - .anthropic.com
      - .openai.com
      - bedrock-runtime.amazonaws.com
      - generativelanguage.googleapis.com
      - api.mistral.ai
      - api.together.xyz
      - api.groq.com
      - api.deepseek.com
  filter_workstation:
    Image|endswith:
      - \chrome.exe
      - \msedge.exe
      - \firefox.exe
      - \Code.exe
      - \slack.exe
      - \Teams.exe
  condition: selection and not filter_workstation
level: high
(source:(cisco.firewall OR linux.syslog OR fortinet.fortigate OR paloaltonetworks.firewall) OR @source.product:(fortigate OR FortiGate OR PAN-OS OR ASA OR FTD)) (@network.destination.port:443 OR @network.protocol:https) (@dns.question.name:(*anthropic.com OR *openai.com OR bedrock-runtime* OR generativelanguage.googleapis.com OR api.mistral.ai OR api.together.xyz OR api.groq.com OR api.deepseek.com) OR @http.url:(*anthropic.com* OR *openai.com* OR *bedrock-runtime* OR *generativelanguage.googleapis.com*) OR @network.destination.domain:(*anthropic.com OR *openai.com))
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, sum(Network_Traffic.bytes_out) as bytes_out, values(Network_Traffic.dest_host) as dest_hosts, values(Network_Traffic.ssl_subject) as sni from datamodel=Network_Traffic where (Network_Traffic.src_category="network_appliance" OR Network_Traffic.src_category="firewall" OR Network_Traffic.src_category="edge_router") Network_Traffic.dest_port=443 by Network_Traffic.src, Network_Traffic.dest_host, _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Network_Traffic)` | search dest_host IN ("*anthropic.com", "*openai.com", "*bedrock-runtime*.amazonaws.com", "*generativelanguage.googleapis.com", "*api.mistral.ai", "*api.together.xyz", "*api.groq.com", "*api.deepseek.com") OR sni IN ("*anthropic.com", "*openai.com") | table _time src dest_host sni count bytes_out
| tstats summariesonly=false count, sum(Network_Traffic.bytes_out) as bytes_out, values(Network_Traffic.dest_host) as dest_hosts, values(Network_Traffic.ssl_subject) as sni from datamodel=Network_Traffic where (Network_Traffic.src_category="network_appliance" OR Network_Traffic.src_category="firewall" OR Network_Traffic.src_category="edge_router") Network_Traffic.dest_port=443 by Network_Traffic.src, Network_Traffic.dest_host, _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Network_Traffic)` | search dest_host IN ("*anthropic.com", "*openai.com", "*bedrock-runtime*.amazonaws.com", "*generativelanguage.googleapis.com", "*api.mistral.ai", "*api.together.xyz", "*api.groq.com", "*api.deepseek.com") OR sni IN ("*anthropic.com", "*openai.com") | table _time src dest_host sni count bytes_out
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("zerodayclock.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["zerodayclock.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with

author: Clankerusecase

detection:

| append

        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS

        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |
    User-driven consent to a third-party OAuth application — illicit-
    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic
    in your SIEM for higher fidelity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

OceanLotus Hits Vietnam Investors With SPECTRALVIPER in FireAnt Attack

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 17 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The Vietnam-aligned threat actor known as OceanLotus has been attributed to two distinct campaigns that targeted domestic entities and stock investors with a backdoor known as SPECTRALVIPER. The campaigns involve a prolonged cyber espionage operation aimed at a Vietnamese infrastructure and transport construction corporation between mid-2024 and February 2026, as well as a supply chain attack

FireAnt Metakit.exe spawns unsigned setup.exe from update path (SPECTRALVIPER supply-chain delivery) AIDelivery High
Catches the FireAnt Metakit update client (Metakit.exe) launching a setup.exe that arrived via the unauthenticated update channel at metakit.fireant[.]vn/Software/version.xml. Article confirms no signature validation on the update binary, so any setup.exe pulled by Metakit.exe is suspect. Rationale: Article names Metakit.exe as the FireAnt update client and setup.exe as the malicious update binary pulled from metakit.fireant[.]vn/Software/version.xml. No signature validation on the update is article-confirmed, so this is a high-fidelity parent/child pair. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine FireAnt Metakit version update where vendor has now signed setup.exe (verify Authenticode + SHA256 vs vendor advisory)
  • FireAnt support tooling that legitimately repackages setup.exe for IT-managed deployments
  • QA/installer test on a developer endpoint inside the FireAnt vendor itself
Suppression filter
and not (SHA256 in ("<vendor-signed-setup-sha256>"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull SHA256 of setup.exe and the network connection that immediately preceded it; check VirusTotal and confirm whether Metakit.exe really contacted metakit.fireant[.]vn/Software/version.xml. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, block financemachinelearning.com and gatewayrvcenter.com at the proxy, and quarantine DtlCrashCatch.dll if found on disk. Step 3 (hunt): Across the estate, sweep for OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe with non-OneDrive parents, the listed SHA1s, and DNS for the article's C2 domains in the prior 6 months — campaign began Oct 2025.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Metakit.exe"
| where FileName =~ "setup.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA1, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\Metakit.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\setup.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DtlCrashCatch.dll image-load by legitimate signed binary (OceanLotus DLL side-load) AIInstallation High
Surfaces the OceanLotus side-loading payload DtlCrashCatch.dll being loaded by a legitimately-signed host binary, which is the bridge between the dropper and SPECTRALVIPER injection into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe. Rationale: DtlCrashCatch.dll is named verbatim in the ESET write-up of the FireAnt SPECTRALVIPER chain — it is the rogue side-loaded DLL and is not a known legitimate Windows / vendor DLL. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/002/
ATT&CKT1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security tool sandbox replaying the malware for analysis (sandbox VM hostnames)
  • Incident-response engineer copying the sample for triage on a forensic workstation
  • Coincidental third-party software shipping a DLL with the same name (none known at time of writing)
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the host binary that loaded DtlCrashCatch.dll and confirm whether it's a signed legitimate binary being abused for side-loading. Step 2 (contain): Quarantine the DLL, snapshot OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe memory, and isolate the host. Step 3 (hunt): Pull the SHA256 of the loading binary across the fleet, sweep for the article's C2 domains in DNS/proxy, and review MSSQL hosts for the parallel transport-construction intrusion pattern.
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated" or EventType == "FileModified"
| where TargetFileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DtlCrashCatch.dll Image Load (SPECTRALVIPER Side-Load)
id: 7b4f9e2a-5d1c-4e83-b6a2-2f1c9d0a4c11
description: DtlCrashCatch.dll is the rogue side-loaded DLL in OceanLotus FireAnt SPECTRALVIPER chain. Any load of this filename is article-specific.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1574.002
logsource:
  category: image_load
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ImageLoaded|endswith: '\DtlCrashCatch.dll'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:7 @ImageLoaded:(*\\DtlCrashCatch.dll OR *\\dtlcrashcatch.dll OR *\\DTLCRASHCATCH.DLL)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\DtlCrashCatch\.dll$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
`sysmon` EventCode=7 ImageLoaded="*\\DtlCrashCatch.dll" | stats min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Image) as host_process values(Hashes) as hashes by host user ImageLoaded | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe spawned/injected outside legitimate OneDrive chain (SPECTRALVIPER injection target) AIInstallation Medium
SPECTRALVIPER hides by injecting into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe. Catches OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe instances whose parent is not the legitimate OneDrive update/launch chain — strong indicator of process hollowing / injection per the article. Rationale: Article explicitly states the side-loaded DLL injects into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe to run SPECTRALVIPER. The legitimate parents of OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe are a known small set — anything else is anomaly-worthy. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1055/012/
ATT&CKT1055.012 T1055
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • First-run OneDrive setup on a freshly imaged machine where MDM tooling launches it
  • OneDrive upgrade where a new bootstrapper not in the allowlist (e.g. new MSIX installer) is the parent
  • Endpoint backup tooling (e.g. Druva, CrashPlan) spawning OneDrive helper processes during snapshot
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName has "setup" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\Microsoft\\OneDrive\\")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Capture the parent process tree and OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe SHA256; confirm whether the binary is the legitimate Microsoft-signed one or a tampered copy. Step 2 (contain): Snapshot OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe memory for SPECTRALVIPER injection artefacts, isolate the host, and block C2 domains financemachinelearning.com and gatewayrvcenter.com. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the parent binary across the fleet, sweep for DtlCrashCatch.dll image-loads, and check whether Metakit.exe is installed on the host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OneDrive.exe","OneDriveSetup.exe","explorer.exe","svchost.exe","StandaloneUpdater.exe","FileCoAuth.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
| where not (ParentProcessName endswith "\\OneDrive.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\OneDriveSetup.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\svchost.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\StandaloneUpdater.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\FileCoAuth.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe OR *\\onedrive.sync.service.exe OR *\\ONEDRIVE.SYNC.SERVICE.EXE) -@ParentImage:(*\\OneDrive.exe OR *\\OneDriveSetup.exe OR *\\explorer.exe OR *\\svchost.exe OR *\\StandaloneUpdater.exe OR *\\FileCoAuth.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\OneDrive\.Sync\.Service\.exe$/i
| NOT (ParentBaseFileName=/^(OneDrive\.exe|OneDriveSetup\.exe|explorer\.exe|svchost\.exe|StandaloneUpdater\.exe|FileCoAuth\.exe)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe" NOT Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OneDrive.exe","OneDriveSetup.exe","explorer.exe","svchost.exe","StandaloneUpdater.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe" NOT Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OneDrive.exe","OneDriveSetup.exe","explorer.exe","svchost.exe","StandaloneUpdater.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
SPECTRALVIPER C2 callout to OceanLotus FireAnt infrastructure AICommand & Control Medium
Network beacon detection for the named OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 domains and IPs from both the FireAnt supply-chain campaign and the Vietnamese transport-construction intrusion. Rationale: All eight IPs and six domains are pre-extracted IOCs for this campaign. financemachinelearning.com and gatewayrvcenter.com are explicitly named in the article body as the SPECTRALVIPER C2 for the FireAnt and transport-construction campaigns respectively. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/ • https://otx.alienvault.com/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platform doing reputation lookups of these exact domains (filter by sandbox/TI VLAN)
  • Researcher / IR analyst manually visiting the indicator (whitelist forensic workstation IPs)
  • DNS sinkhole/passive-DNS infrastructure that resolves these names for telemetry
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") and AccountName in~ ("<soc-analyst-accounts>"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the initiating process on the host; if not a browser launched by an analyst, treat as confirmed beacon. Step 2 (contain): Block all six domains and eight IPs at the proxy/firewall, isolate the host, and quarantine any DtlCrashCatch.dll. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep 6 months of DNS/proxy for any of these indicators, pivot to other hosts contacting the same /24, and check MSSQL hosts for the parallel transport-construction intrusion.
let badDomains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let badIPs = dynamic(["38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(180d)
| where RemoteIP in (badIPs) or RemoteUrl has_any (badDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let badDomains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let badIPs = dynamic(["38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
  | where DestinationIP in (badIPs) or RequestURL has_any (badDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (badDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DeviceProduct),
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
  | where Name has_any (badDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Public-facing MSSQL sqlservr.exe spawns suspicious child (OceanLotus transport-construction intrusion vector) AIExploitation High
Catches the suspected initial access pathway into the Vietnamese transport-construction firm: RCE against a public-facing MSSQL server leading to sqlservr.exe spawning a scripting/utility child — the OceanLotus foothold before SPECTRALVIPER side-load. Rationale: Article explicitly identifies exploitation of RCE in public-facing MSSQL as the suspected initial access for the transport-construction intrusion. sqlservr.exe spawning any of these LOLBins is the textbook xp_cmdshell/sp_OACreate footprint. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.003 T1505.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DBA running ad-hoc xp_cmdshell for maintenance (rare — should be disabled per policy)
  • SQL Server Agent jobs intentionally calling shell tooling (whitelist by job-account SID)
  • Monitoring agent that piggybacks on sqlservr.exe for inventory collection
Suppression filter
and not (AccountName in~ ("<dba-service-account>") and ProcessCommandLine has "backup")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full xp_cmdshell / sp_OACreate audit trail and identify the SQL login that issued the command; check whether MSSQL is internet-exposed. Step 2 (contain): Block inbound 1433/1434 at the perimeter, disable xp_cmdshell on the affected instance, rotate the sa / SQL service-account passwords, and isolate the host. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep for OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe with non-OneDrive parents, DtlCrashCatch.dll image-loads, and DNS to gatewayrvcenter.com across all MSSQL hosts and adjacent subnets.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(180d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "sqlservr.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","setup.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\sqlservr.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\bitsadmin.exe","\\certutil.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe","\\net.exe","\\net1.exe","\\whoami.exe","\\setup.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SPECTRALVIPER known-bad SHA1 observed on disk or in process AIInstallation High
Direct hash-match alert on the five SHA1s tied by ESET to the OceanLotus FireAnt SPECTRALVIPER components. Cheap to deploy, high fidelity. Rationale: The five SHA1s are pre-extracted from the article's IOC bundle for this exact campaign. Hash hits do not need behavioural context to be high-confidence. Cross-checked against: • https://otx.alienvault.com/ • https://www.virustotal.com/
ATT&CKT1027 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel sandbox detonating the sample on instrumented VMs
  • IR/forensic analyst storing the binary on a forensic workstation for triage
  • AV signature update where the vendor packages the hash as a sample
Suppression filter
and not (DeviceName in ("<sandbox-hostnames>","<forensic-workstations>"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull host context — is this a forensic/sandbox VM or a production endpoint? Step 2 (contain): If production, isolate immediately, snapshot OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe memory, and block financemachinelearning.com / gatewayrvcenter.com. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the user, parent process, and immediate predecessor download URL; sweep adjacent hosts for the article's C2 indicators.

(DeviceFileEvents   | where Timestamp > ago(365d) | where SHA1 in (badSHA1) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in (badSHA1) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
(DeviceImageLoadEvents | where Timestamp > ago(365d) | where SHA1 in (badSHA1) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName)
| order by Timestamp desc
let badSHA1 = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D","B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194","48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947","511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB","8CD78B8DB76563e4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);

(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(365d)

Registry Run-key persistence written by SPECTRALVIPER side-load chain AIInstallation Medium
Persistence on a host where DtlCrashCatch.dll was loaded or OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe was injected — detects Run/RunOnce writes whose data points back to the side-load directory of the OceanLotus chain. Rationale: Run-key write referencing DtlCrashCatch (the named rogue DLL) or OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe in Temp/ProgramData is article-specific. Filename references come directly from the ESET-reported chain. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/
ATT&CKT1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate OneDrive setup writing a Run value pointing at OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe (filtered by OneDriveSetup.exe parent)
  • Software installer dropping into ProgramData and registering a Run entry (vendor-signed)
  • Endpoint backup agent re-registering itself after upgrade
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\Microsoft\\OneDrive\\" and InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has "Microsoft")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Resolve the Run-key data to a binary on disk and pull its SHA256 and Authenticode signature. Step 2 (contain): Delete the autostart entry, isolate the host, and quarantine the referenced binary plus any DtlCrashCatch.dll on disk. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the same value-data path across the fleet, sweep for the article's C2 domains in DNS, and check whether Metakit.exe or sqlservr.exe was the original parent.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(180d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run","\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("DtlCrashCatch","OneDrive.Sync.Service","\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\","\\ProgramData\\")
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OneDriveSetup.exe","OneDrive.exe","msiexec.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
| where EventType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run","\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("DtlCrashCatch","OneDrive.Sync.Service","\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\","\\ProgramData\\")
| where not (ActingProcessName has_any ("OneDriveSetup.exe","OneDrive.exe","msiexec.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SPECTRALVIPER Side-Load Persistence via Run Key
id: e7d3c901-5a2c-4b8e-91f7-3a2e1d8c0b22
description: Run/RunOnce write whose value data points at DtlCrashCatch / OneDrive.Sync.Service / Temp-or-ProgramData paths consistent with the OceanLotus FireAnt chain
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1547.001
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_key:
    TargetObject|contains:
      - '\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\'
      - '\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce\'
  selection_value:
    Details|contains:
      - 'DtlCrashCatch'
      - 'OneDrive.Sync.Service'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
  filter:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\OneDriveSetup.exe'
      - '\OneDrive.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
  condition: selection_key and selection_value and not filter
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\* OR *\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce\\* OR *\\currentversion\\run\\* OR *\\currentversion\\runonce\\*) @Details:(*DtlCrashCatch* OR *dtlcrashcatch* OR *OneDrive.Sync.Service* OR *\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\*) -@Image:(*\\OneDriveSetup.exe OR *\\OneDrive.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| RegObjectName=/\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\(Run|RunOnce)/i
| RegStringValue=/(DtlCrashCatch|OneDrive\.Sync\.Service|\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\|\\ProgramData\\)/i
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\\(OneDriveSetup|OneDrive|msiexec)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegObjectName, RegValueName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path IN ("*\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\*","*\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce\\*") (Registry.registry_value_data="*DtlCrashCatch*" OR Registry.registry_value_data="*OneDrive.Sync.Service*" OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*" OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\\ProgramData\\*\\setup.exe*") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path IN ("*\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\*","*\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce\\*") (Registry.registry_value_data="*DtlCrashCatch*" OR Registry.registry_value_data="*OneDrive.Sync.Service*" OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*" OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\\ProgramData\\*\\setup.exe*") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that

references:

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

      AND (Filesystem.file_name IN ("metakit.exe","dtlcrashcatch.dll","onedrive.sync.service.exe"))
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FireAnt Metakit supply-chain — malicious update spawning suspicious child
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — OceanLotus: From external espionage to domestic targeting
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER known-bad SHA1 — file write or execution on disk · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 — outbound to known C&C IPs · [LLM] OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 — DNS queries to known C&C domains · [LLM] OceanLotus historical C2 — DNS tunneling to unusually long subdomain (Denis/SOUNDBITE) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 — outbound to known C&C IPs AICommand & Control Medium
Detects outbound network connections from endpoints to the SPECTRALVIPER C&C infrastructure published in ESET's June 2026 OceanLotus write-up. High-fidelity IP-IOC match — any production endpoint touching this list during the campaign window (mid-2024 → Mar 2026 and onward) is almost certainly OceanLotus traffic. Rationale: All eight IPs are taken verbatim from the article body and Table 2 (C&C mapping). Four of them (139.180.128.42, 139.99.33.239, 166.88.77.186, 103.119.47.104) are explicitly tied in Table 2 to SPECTRALVIPER C&C domains; the remaining four appear in the IOC bundle. IP-IOC matches are inherently high-fidelity — these are dedicated attacker VPS endpoints, not shared CDN infrastructure. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / sandbox reanalyzing the same ESET IOCs from a corporate workstation
  • Threat-intel platform polling these IPs to verify reachability (TIP enrichment)
  • Penetration test using the same indicators as test C2
  • Honeyclient / detonation VM with internet access generating connections during analysis
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("explorer.exe")
// only suppress legit-browser hits if your TIP intentionally browses to these IPs
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the initiating process tree on the affected DeviceId — confirm the binary is not a known scanner/sandbox/TIP enrichment job; capture the parent SHA256. Step 2 (contain): isolate the device via Defender ASR / Falcon RTR; block the matched IP and the four sibling C&C IPs at the perimeter firewall and EDR network containment. Step 3 (hunt): retro-search 30 days of DeviceNetworkEvents/Sysmon EID 3 across the fleet for the same C2 IPs and the six C&C domains (Table 2); pivot on InitiatingProcessSHA256 to find sister implants on other hosts; sweep for any of the 20 SPECTRALVIPER SHA1s in DeviceFileEvents.
let OceanLotusC2 = dynamic(["139.162.11.152","142.91.98.77","139.180.128.42","139.99.33.239","166.88.77.186","103.119.47.104","38.60.245.37","194.68.26.241"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (OceanLotusC2)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let OceanLotusC2 = dynamic(["139.162.11.152","142.91.98.77","139.180.128.42","139.99.33.239","166.88.77.186","103.119.47.104","38.60.245.37","194.68.26.241"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in (OceanLotusC2)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
